name: Long Call into Earnings (IV expansion play)
summary: Buy a call ahead of an earnings release to profit from a post-report gap. Included for completeness and clearly marked a BAD IDEA in its naive form: IV crush usually beats the move.

legs.dte_rule: first expiry AFTER the earnings date, typically 2-9 DTE

max_profit: Unlimited in theory; in practice capped by how far the gap exceeds the priced-in expected move
max_loss: Debit x 100. Loss is the base case - post-report IV collapse routinely removes 30-60% of the option's value even when direction is right.
breakevens: strike + debit; compare to the option-implied expected move. If breakeven is beyond the expected move, the trade is priced against you

greeks.vega: positive and TOXIC here - you are buying vega at its annual peak and it collapses the morning after

typical_dte: 2-9 DTE (the expiry immediately after the report)
when_to_use: Almost never in the naive form. Only defensible when front-month IV is NOT elevated versus its own earnings history (current earnings IV below the trailing 8-quarter median) and you have a genuine directional edge.
entry_rules: Gate: current front-expiry IV must be BELOW the median IV of the last 8 earnings cycles for that name. If above, do not take the trade
Compute the option-implied expected move = 0.85 x (ATM straddle price). Require your directional target to exceed that move, otherwise skip
Debit <= 0.3% of equity (~$150 on $50k); max 2 earnings positions per quarter
Delta 0.30-0.45, first expiry after the report
Liquid names only: OI >= 1000, spread <= 8% of mid
Mark this strategy DISABLED by default in the automation config; require an explicit manual enable per trade
management_rules: Exit within the first 30 minutes of the session after the report. The edge, if any, is in the gap, not the drift
Stop at -50% or at the 30-minute mark, whichever first
Never hold a post-earnings long option for a second day
exit_rules: Sell to close by 10:00 ET on the session after the report, unconditionally
Standard 15:30 ET expiry-day flatten applies if it somehow survives to expiry
liquidity_needs: Post-earnings open spreads blow out; require a first-5-minute check that the spread has normalised to <= 10% of mid before exiting.
common_mistakes: Being right on direction and still losing money to IV crush - the single most common retail options loss; buying the weekly the day before the report when IV is at its annual maximum.
